newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: GUATEMALA EXPORTS UP 16 PERCENT THROUGH MAY 1997.
newsitem.headline: GUATEMALA EXPORTS UP 16 PERCENT THROUGH MAY 1997.

text.p: Guatemalan exports for the first five months of 1997 showed a 16 percent increase over the same period last year, the Central Bank said on Wednesday.

Exports for January through May 1997 were $1.08 billion, $147 million higher than during the same period of 1996, according to the bank's "Principal Foreign Export Statistics" publication made available to Reuters on Wednesday.
High world coffee prices combined with a record-breaking coffee production year meant a 34.3 percent raise in the total value of Guatemala's coffee exports.
Guatemala exported $349 million worth of coffee in the first five months of the year compared to $260 million last year.

The value of sugar and banana exports, Guatemala's second-and third-lace exports, were down nine and five percent respectively, in the January-May period. Sugar brought in $138 million in the first five months of this year while bananas accounted for $55 million.
Meat exports showed a dramatic drop of 74 percent, from $1 million to $313 thousand, while petroleum exports were up 138 percent, from $18 million to $42 million.

Petroleum became Guatemala's fourth-largest export product, overtaking cardamom, which represented $19 million worth of exports during the first five months of this year and the same amount from January-May last year.
Guatemala's production of crude oil -- all of which is exported -- has doubled since 1995 to 23,000 barrels a day.

The United States continued to be the largest market for Guatemalan products, absorbing $383 million worth of exports. El Salvador is the second-largest importer of Guatemalan products at $119 million.
Exports to other Central American countries as a whole (Costa Rica, El Salvador, Honduras and Nicaragua) were worth $261 million through May of this year.
